projects.jlptLabSubtitle: Daily AI experimentation and research used to explore new tools, workflows, and use cases for the team.

overview.title: Project Overview
overview.p1: This project covers my ongoing work as an AI Researcher at Hurdman.
overview.p2: The goal is to explore what current AI tools can actually do in practice, beyond the marketing claims. That means using them daily, comparing models, and seeing how each one handles real workflows.
overview.p3: Instead of treating AI as a single tool, I look at it as a moving ecosystem where new capabilities and trade-offs appear every week. Tracking that change is part of the job.
overview.p4: The findings feed into how the team thinks about automation, content, and product direction.

coreIdea.title: Core Concept
coreIdea.p1: At the heart of this work is a simple question: where does AI actually move the needle?
coreIdea.p2: Rather than chasing every trend, the focus is on hands-on experimentation. I test tools against concrete tasks, compare outputs, document what works, and write up what doesn't. The aim is practical insight the team can use, not a hype recap.

userFriendly.title: How It's Shared
userFriendly.p1: The research is built to be easy to consume.
userFriendly.p2: I create and edit short videos, written summaries, and side-by-side comparisons so the team can absorb findings quickly without having to run every experiment themselves. The format is designed to keep knowledge moving across the team.

status.title: Current Status
status.p1: The research is ongoing and updated continuously.
status.p2: New tools, models, and use cases are added as they appear, with priorities shifting based on what the team and product need most at any given time.

purpose.title: Project Purpose
purpose.p1: The purpose of this work is to keep Hurdman ahead of the curve on AI: which tools to adopt, which to skip, and how to apply them in ways that produce real, repeatable results.
